1.word_for_word: विमोहन्[अहि]{।मर्क्}-दण्डेन — the electronic source begins with a corrupt bracketed reading; ततः स्वान् शरणागतान् गोपान् — thereafter his own cowherds who had taken refuge in him; अपात् — he protected; अनन्तः असौ — that Infinite One; अनन्त-वन-वह्नितः — from the boundless forest fire; अष्टादशे — in the eighteenth chapter; ग्रीष्मे वसन्त-गुण-लक्षिते — in summer marked by the qualities of spring; अघातयत् बलेन — he caused Balarāma to kill; प्रलम्बम् — Pralamba; लीलया हरिः — Hari, in sport; कृत्वा नृत्यं फणाग्रेषु कालियस्य — having danced upon the tips of Kāliya's hoods; स-कौतुकम् — playfully; बलं प्रलम्ब-तुङ्ग-अंसम् आरोहयत् — he caused Bala to mount Pralamba's lofty shoulder; अरातिहा — the destroyer of enemies
1.translation: The electronic source opens with a corrupt bracketed reading, which is therefore not silently emended. The readable summary states: thereafter that Infinite One protected his own cowherds, who had taken refuge in him, from the boundless forest fire. In the eighteenth chapter, during a summer that displayed the qualities of spring, Hari playfully caused Pralamba to be killed by Bala. Having sportfully danced upon the tips of Kāliya's hoods, the destroyer of enemies caused Bala to mount Pralamba's lofty shoulder.

2.word_for_word: गोपाल-च्छद्म-माया — the māyā whose disguise was that of a cowherd; गो-पालनम् एव च्छद्म यस्याम् — in which the very act of tending cows was the disguise; तया मायया — by that māyā
2.translation: ‘Gopāla-cchadma-māyā’ means the māyā whose disguise was that of a cowherd—the very act of tending cows served as its disguise.

4.word_for_word: वसन्त-साम्यम् आह चतुर्भिः — in four verses he states its similarity to spring; ग्रीष्मे अपि — even in summer; निर्झराणां निर्ह्रादेन घोषेण — by the roar and sound of the waterfalls; निवृत्त-स्वनाः छन्न-ध्वनयः झिल्लिकाः — the harsh sounds of the cicadas were suppressed and covered; कठोर-ध्वनि-सूक्ष्म-कीटाः — the tiny insects of harsh sound; शश्वत् निर्झराणां शीकरैः — continually by droplets from the waterfalls; ऋजीषाः स्निग्धाः द्रुमाः — the trees were moist and glossy; तेषां मण्डलैः मण्डितम् — adorned with their circles or groves
4.translation: In four verses he describes how the summer resembled spring. Even in summer, the roar of the waterfalls drowned out the harsh sound of the cicadas, those tiny insects with piercing voices. Moreover, the trees were continually moistened and made glossy by droplets from the waterfalls, and Vṛndāvana was adorned by circles and groves of such trees.

5.word_for_word: यत्र ग्रीष्मे वने वा — there, in summer, or in that forest; निदाघः ग्रीष्मः — nidāgha means summer heat; तत्-कालीन-वह्नि-अर्काभ्यां भवति दवः तापः — the burning heat produced by the seasonal fire and sun; अति-शाद्वले — exceedingly covered with green grass; अति-हरित-तृण-आकीर्णे — strewn with very green grass; यद् वा — or; अतिक्रान्त-शाद्वले अपि स्थाने — even in a place beyond the grassy tract
5.translation: ‘Nidāgha’ means the summer heat, and ‘dava’ here is the burning produced by the fire and sun of that season. ‘Ati-śādvale’ may mean a place thickly covered with exceptionally green grass; alternatively it may refer even to a place beyond the grassy tract.

6.word_for_word: ननु शाद्वलम् एव कुतस्त्यम् — but how could such grass exist there at all; अगाध-तोयाः ह्रदिन्यः — pools of unfathomable water; तट-स्पर्शिभिः ऊर्मिभिः — by waves touching their banks; पुलिनैः सह द्रवत्-पुरीषं पङ्कः यस्याः भुवः — the earth whose mud remained flowing/moist along the sandy banks; रसं शाद्वलितम् — its moisture became grassy growth; चण्डांशु-कराः सूर्य-रश्मयः — the fierce rays of the sun; विषवत् उल्बणाः अपि — though intense like poison; न गृह्णते न हरन्ति — could not seize or remove it
6.translation: An objection is raised: how could there be grassy ground in such a season? The answer is that the pools contained unfathomably deep water; their waves touched the banks, keeping the earth and its mud moist even along the sandy stretches. Thus the earth retained the moisture from which the grass arose, and even the fierce, poison-like rays of the sun could not absorb or carry it away.

7.word_for_word: तद् वनम् अविशत् — he entered that forest; इति उत्तरेण अन्वयः — this is construed with what follows; नदन्तः चित्राः मृगाः द्विजाः च यस्मिन् — where various deer and birds cried out; गायन्तः मयूराः भ्रमराः च यस्मिन् — where peacocks and bees sang; कूजन्तः कोकिलाः सारसाः च यस्मिन् — where cuckoos and cranes called; तत् अविशत् — he entered that forest
7.translation: The words are to be connected with what follows: he entered that forest in which many kinds of deer and birds gave their cries, in which peacocks and bees seemed to sing, and in which cuckoos and cranes called. This construction extends through verse 11.

12.word_for_word: काक-पक्षाः — side-locks called kāka-pakṣa; चूडा-करणात् प्राक्तन-केशाः — hair remaining before the cūḍākaraṇa ceremony; भ्रामण-आदि-प्रकारैः — by methods such as whirling; नियुद्धेन बाहु-युद्धेन — by wrestling, combat with the arms; चिक्रीडतुः — the two played
12.translation: ‘Kāka-pakṣa’ refers to the side-locks of hair worn before the cūḍākaraṇa ceremony. The two boys played by wrestling—arm-to-arm combat—using movements such as whirling one another around. The explanation carries into verse 13.

14.word_for_word: कुम्भैः — with kumbha fruits; कुम्भ-वृक्ष-फलैः — the fruits of the kumbha tree; अस्पृश्यत्वम् — the game of remaining untouchable; नेत्र-बन्धः — blindfolding the eyes; तद्-आद्यैः — and similar games; मृगाणां स्व-गाणां च चेष्टया — by imitating the movements of animals and of their own groups
14.translation: ‘Kumbhaiḥ’ means with fruits of the kumbha tree. Their games included keeping oneself from being touched, blindfolding the eyes and similar sports, as well as imitating the movements of animals and of their companions.

15.word_for_word: दर्दुर-प्लावैः — with frog-jumps; मण्डूक-प्लुतिभिः — leaps like frogs; स्पृन्दोलिकया — with the swinging game; कोलालम्बनेन — hanging/swinging while holding on; नृपाणाम् इव लीलया — with sport like that of kings
15.translation: ‘Dardura-plāvaiḥ’ means leaps like frogs. ‘Spṛndolikā’ is a swinging game, hanging and swinging while holding on. They also played in a manner like the sport of kings.

16.word_for_word: नद्यः — rivers; अद्रि-द्रोण्यः — mountain valleys or hollows; कुञ्जानि च — and bowers; एतेषु — in these places
16.translation: The places meant are rivers, mountain valleys or hollows, and forest bowers.

17.word_for_word: चारयतोः सतोः — while the two were tending the animals; तद्-वने तस्मिन् वने — in that forest; तयोः जिहीर्षया — with a desire to carry the two of them away
17.translation: While the two boys were tending the animals in that forest, Pralamba entered with a desire to carry them away. The construction continues through verse 18.

19.word_for_word: यथा-यथम् — each according to what was appropriate; वयः-बल-आदि-अनुरूपम् — in accordance with age, strength and the like; द्वन्द्वी-भूय — forming pairs for contests
19.translation: They formed pairs for the contests, each matched appropriately according to age, strength and the like.

20.word_for_word: परिवृढौ — the two leaders; नायकौ — chiefs; केचन कृष्ण-सङ्घट्टिनः — some joined with Kṛṣṇa; कृष्ण-पक्षीयाः — members of Kṛṣṇa's side
20.translation: ‘Parivṛḍhau’ means the two leaders, the chiefs. Of the boys, some joined with Kṛṣṇa and belonged to Kṛṣṇa's side. The explanation continues through verse 21.

22.word_for_word: वाह्यमानाः — being carried; पृष्ठे — on the back; ऊह्यमानाः — being borne along
22.translation: ‘Vāhyamānāḥ’ means being carried—being borne along on another's back. The explanation applies through verse 24.

25.word_for_word: कृष्ण-दृष्टि-वञ्चनाय — in order to evade Kṛṣṇa's sight; अवरुह्यते अस्मिन् इति अवरोहणम् — the prescribed point at which one dismounts; मर्यादा — the boundary or limit; ततः परं दूरम् अगात् — he went far beyond that point
25.translation: To evade Kṛṣṇa's notice, Pralamba went past the ‘avarohaṇa,’ the prescribed boundary at which the rider was to dismount, and proceeded far beyond it.

26.word_for_word: धरणि-धर-इन्द्रवत् गौरवं यस्य — whose weight was like that of the lord of mountains; निजम् आसुरं वपुः आस्थितः — he assumed his own demonic body; पुरट-परिच्छदः — adorned with gold; सुवर्ण-अलङ्कारः — with golden ornaments; तडित्-द्युमान् — shining like lightning; विद्युत्-दीप्तिमान् — lightning-bright; उडुपति-वाट् — bearing the lord of stars, the moon; राम-उपमा — a comparison involving Rāma; यदि विद्युतः यथोचित-स्थानेषु स्थिताः उपरि उडुपतिः — if lightning is situated appropriately and the moon is above; सः अम्बुदः यथा भाति — as such a cloud appears; तद्वत् बभौ — so he appeared
26.translation: Pralamba assumed his own demonic body, whose weight was like that of the lord of mountains. ‘Puraṭa-paricchada’ means adorned with golden ornaments, and ‘taḍid-dyumān’ means shining like lightning. The phrase about bearing the lord of stars supplies a comparison involving Rāma: just as a dark cloud appears when lightning flashes in the proper places and the moon is borne above it, so Pralamba appeared while carrying Balarāma.

27.word_for_word: अलम् — exceedingly; अतिवेगेन — with very great speed; प्रदीप्ते दृशौ यस्मिन् — whose two eyes blazed; भ्रु-कुटि-तट-सल्लग्नाः उग्राः दंष्ट्राः — whose terrible fangs reached the ridge of his knitted brows; प्रदीप्त-दृक् भ्रु-कुटि-तटम् — with the brow-ridge around blazing eyes; ज्वलन्त्यः शिखाः केशाः यस्मिन् — whose hair-locks blazed like flames
27.translation: ‘Alam’ here intensifies the description: he moved with tremendous speed. His two eyes blazed; his terrible fangs rose toward the ridge formed by his contracted brows, and his locks of hair seemed to burn like tongues of flame. The Sanskrit also allows the blazing eyes and brow-ridge to be taken together as one descriptive compound.

28.word_for_word: आगत-स्मृतिः — his awareness having returned; अभयः इव — as if fearless; आत्मनः सार्थं गोप-समूहं विहाय — having left his own caravan, the group of cowherds; हरन्तं रिपुम् — the enemy carrying him away; अहनत् — he struck; यद् वा — or; विहायसा आकाश-मार्गेण — by the path of the sky; आत्मनः प्राप्तम् अर्थम् इव हरन्तम् — carrying away as though a prize he had obtained; वज्र-रंहसा मुष्टिना — with a fist having the speed and force of a thunderbolt
28.translation: When Balarāma regained his composure, he became as if completely fearless and struck the enemy who, after leaving behind Balarāma's own company of cowherds, was carrying him away. Alternatively, the construction may mean that the demon was carrying Balarāma through the sky as though carrying off a prize he had obtained. Balarāma struck him with a fist possessing the speed and force of a thunderbolt.

29.word_for_word: अपस्मृतः — deprived of consciousness; गत-स्मृतिः — his awareness gone; महा-रवम् समीरयन् — sending forth a tremendous roar
29.translation: ‘Apasmṛta’ means that his consciousness was gone. He sent forth a tremendous roar. The explanation carries through verse 30.

31.word_for_word: तद्-अर्हणम् — honoring him for that deed; प्रशंसा-अर्हम् — worthy of praise
31.translation: ‘Tad-arhaṇam’ means honoring him for that deed, which was worthy of praise. The explanation carries through verse 32.
